MARKET OVERVIEW

1. What is the Current Market Regime?
NEUTRAL: normal volatility at 32.2% and mixed breadth, with 4/8 sectors positive. The split in sector performance, alongside negative one-month returns across all sectors, argues for selectivity.

2. Which sectors are leading?
Technology & Telecom leads (1W: +21.46% | 1M: -6.32%), in RECOVERY, with KONTR (1W: +58.99% | 1M: -5.56%) and TCELL (1W: +3.76% | 1M: -4.09%) in RECOVERY. Construction & REIT (1W: +1.94% | 1M: -12.11%) and Transportation (1W: +1.66% | 1M: -6.35%) are also in RECOVERY.

3. Which sectors are lagging?
Holding & Investment is weakest (1W: -2.79% | 1M: -7.94%), BELOW TREND; Energy & Chemicals (1W: -2.29% | 1M: -18.14%) and Banking & Finance (1W: -1.91% | 1M: -4.86%) are also BELOW TREND. Energy’s monthly decline is the deepest, while Retail & Food remains BELOW TREND (1W: -0.50% | 1M: -9.89%).

STOCK PERFORMANCE

4. Top Performing Stocks?
KONTR (1W: +58.99% | 1M: -5.56%), TKFEN (1W: +6.83% | 1M: -23.06%), KRDMD (1W: +6.32% | 1M: -11.41%), ENKAI (1W: +6.30% | 1M: -4.52%) and AEFES (1W: +5.06% | 1M: -7.05%) are all in RECOVERY. KONTR’s outsized weekly gain leads, but its negative monthly return means the bounce is not yet a trend reversal.

5. Worst Performing Stocks?
SOKM (1W: -8.94% | 1M: -8.22%), HALKB (1W: -7.41% | 1M: -10.49%), TUPRS (1W: -7.20% | 1M: -10.28%), SAHOL (1W: -5.77% | 1M: -4.90%) and TRALT (1W: -4.26% | 1M: -21.14%) are all BELOW TREND. Weakness spans retail, banking, energy and holdings.

6. Momentum Stocks?
The strongest weekly momentum is concentrated in KONTR (1W: +58.99% | 1M: -5.56%), TKFEN (1W: +6.83% | 1M: -23.06%) and KRDMD (1W: +6.32% | 1M: -11.41%), all in RECOVERY. Their monthly losses keep the moves in bounce territory rather than confirmed uptrends.

SECTOR OUTLOOK

7. Banking Sector Outlook?
Banking & Finance is BELOW TREND (1W: -1.91% | 1M: -4.86%). AKBNK (1W: -4.23% | 1M: -7.23%) and YKBNK (1W: -3.18% | 1M: -0.69%) are BELOW TREND, while ISCTR (1W: +0.41% | 1M: -1.12%) and TSKB (1W: +2.33% | 1M: -6.59%) are in RECOVERY.

8. Industrial Sector Outlook?
Heavy Industry is in RECOVERY at the sector level (1W: +0.39% | 1M: -15.28%), but the monthly decline remains pronounced. KRDMD (1W: +6.32% | 1M: -11.41%), ASELS (1W: +2.24% | 1M: -5.58%) and EREGL (1W: +0.13% | 1M: -16.53%) are in RECOVERY; FROTO (1W: -2.72% | 1M: -10.86%) is BELOW TREND.

9. Energy & Chemicals Outlook?
Energy & Chemicals remains BELOW TREND (1W: -2.29% | 1M: -18.14%). TUPRS (1W: -7.20% | 1M: -10.28%) and SASA (1W: -3.85% | 1M: -22.28%) are BELOW TREND, with no clear sector-wide stabilization signal.

PORTFOLIO STRATEGY

10. Portfolio Recommendation?
Maintain a balanced, cautious stance in the NEUTRAL regime; avoid broad risk increases while breadth is mixed and sector one-month returns remain negative. Favor selective exposure to relative weekly leaders, with position sizing disciplined given their RECOVERY—not ABOVE TREND—status.

NEXT WEEK OUTLOOK

11. Stocks to Watch Next Week?
Monitor KONTR (1W: +58.99% | 1M: -5.56%) for follow-through after its sharp surge, and TKFEN (1W: +6.83% | 1M: -23.06%) for evidence its bounce can persist. KRDMD (1W: +6.32% | 1M: -11.41%), ENKAI (1W: +6.30% | 1M: -4.52%) and TCELL (1W: +3.76% | 1M: -4.09%) are also in RECOVERY and worth tracking for momentum confirmation.

12. Sectors to Watch Next Week?
Technology & Telecom leads the weekly rebound but remains in RECOVERY (1W: +21.46% | 1M: -6.32%); monitor whether gains broaden beyond its leaders. Energy & Chemicals (1W: -2.29% | 1M: -18.14%) and Banking & Finance (1W: -1.91% | 1M: -4.86%) remain BELOW TREND and are key downside-risk gauges.

13. Key Levels & Triggers?
No XU100 spot, support or resistance levels were provided, so specific index levels cannot be stated. Watch for improvement in breadth beyond 4/8 sectors and sustained weekly gains alongside recovering monthly returns as confirmation; renewed volatility or further breadth deterioration would be a caution signal.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The market is NEUTRAL, with normal volatility and mixed breadth; weekly strength is led by Technology & Telecom, while every sector remains negative on a one-month basis. Favor selective recovery candidates over broad exposure, and treat energy and banking weakness—and the possibility that sharp rebounds fade—as key risks.
